'''''Sagina apetala''''' is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Caryophyllaceae]] known by the common names '''annual pearlwort'''<ref>{{PLANTS|id=SAAP|taxon=Sagina apetala|accessdate=26 October 2015}}</ref> and '''dwarf pearlwort'''. It is native to Europe and it is known elsewhere as an [[introduced species]], including parts of North America. It grows in many types of disturbed habitat, such as cracks in the sidewalk. It is a petite annual herb producing a threadlike stem just a few centimeters long, spreading or growing erect. The plant is glandular and somewhat hairy. The leaves are linear in shape and not more than about a centimeter long. The [[inflorescence]] is a solitary flower borne on a threadlike [[Pedicel (botany)|pedicel]]. The flower has usually four [[sepal]]s and generally no petals.
